## Your route {#route}

**What exactly repeats, and how will we know whether every request was handled?**

Week 11 isolated a rule and checked it on chosen inputs. Week 12 repeats a
checked descriptive calculation across named columns. A loop is not a shortcut
around understanding the function: it repeats both its strengths and its bugs.

We use the built-in `airquality` data throughout. First convert a whole vector,
then compare list results, typed scalar results and a loop. Finally request both
valid and invalid columns and keep a complete record of every request.

::: {.callout-note #words}
## Words used in this chapter

| Word or pattern | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Vectorization** | Apply an operation already defined for a whole vector to all its elements. |
| **Iteration** | Repeat a workflow for each declared input, here a column name. |
| **Scalar** | One value, such as one mean. |
| **List** | A container keeping one possibly structured object per input. |
| **`[[name]]`** | Select the column whose name is stored in the object `name`. |
| **Output template** | The type and length each call must return; `numeric(1)` requests one number. |
| **Preallocation** | Create the result container with its intended size and type before filling it. |
| **Status row** | One record saying which request ran, whether it succeeded and what failed. |
| **Coercion** | Changing values to a common type, for example numbers becoming text. |
| **`NA_real_` / `NA_character_`** | Missing values explicitly typed as numeric or character. |
:::

## Meeting 1 · Read the computation {#meeting-one}

Class route: two 75-minute meetings, each with its final five-minute exit.

The question has two different levels. `(Temp - 32) * 5 / 9` converts each
of 153 temperatures; R already applies the arithmetic element by element.
`variables <- c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")` instead declares four
requests, each asking a function to examine a complete column. Keep the number
of observations separate from the number of repeated tasks.

### One vector, four variables, three ways to repeat {#stage-1}

**Slide cues:** *Vectorize Elementwise Work*; *Select By A Stored Name*; *`lapply`: One Object Per Input*; *`vapply`: State The Type*; *Compare Behavior*.

`data[[variable_name]]` selects a column by a stored name; `$variable_name`
would seek a literal column called `variable_name`. Before automating anything,
read `summarize_numeric` as a contract: it accepts a data frame and one present,
numeric column with at least one observed value. It returns one row containing
the variable name, total and missing counts, mean and standard deviation.

The function first builds `observed`; the mean is over those values, while
`n_total` still counts every day. `lapply` keeps a list of four one-row tables;
`bind_rows` combines them. `vapply(..., numeric(1))` instead requires one number
per variable and preserves the character input names. The preallocated loop
fills a named numeric vector and is checked against that result.

**Predict in a private comment first:** Will the temperature conversion return four values or 153? How many elements will the list of variable summaries contain?

<details>
<summary>Compare your reasoning</summary>

The converted vector has 153 values, one per day. The summary list has four
elements, one per requested variable. If your answer differed, you probably
counted observations when the iteration inputs were column names, or vice versa.

</details>

**Try before expanding:** For the Core 2/4 work, sketch which expression acts on the whole vector and which repeats over names. If attempting the function, start with its signature and validation comments before comparing the full version.

<details>
<summary>Reference version · week12-vectorized-iteration_sol.R</summary>

```{r}
#| label: w12-reference-1
# MATH 346 - possible worked solution
# Compare only after attempting the starter; other correct implementations are possible.

library(dplyr)

data <- airquality |>
  mutate(day_id = row_number())

variables <- c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")

# Vectorize an elementwise calculation instead of looping over observations.
temperature_c <- (data$Temp - 32) * 5 / 9

stopifnot(
  length(temperature_c) == nrow(data),
  abs(temperature_c[1] - 19.4444444444444) < 1e-10,
  !any(is.na(temperature_c))
)

summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("data must be a data frame")
  }
  if (!is.character(variable_name) || length(variable_name) != 1) {
    stop("variable_name must be one character value")
  }
  if (!variable_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("requested variable is not present")
  }

  values <- data[[variable_name]]
  if (!is.numeric(values)) {
    stop("requested variable must be numeric")
  }

  observed <- values[!is.na(values)]
  if (length(observed) == 0) {
    stop("requested variable has no observed values")
  }

  tibble(
    variable = variable_name,
    n_total = length(values),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(values)),
    mean = mean(observed),
    standard_deviation = sd(observed)
  )
}

# lapply keeps one result object for every requested input.
summary_list <- lapply(
  variables,
  function(variable_name) summarize_numeric(data, variable_name)
)
summary_table <- bind_rows(summary_list)

stopifnot(
  nrow(summary_table) == length(variables),
  identical(summary_table$variable, variables),
  identical(summary_table$n_missing, c(37L, 7L, 0L, 0L))
)

# vapply states that every iteration must return exactly one number.
means_vapply <- vapply(
  variables,
  function(variable_name) mean(data[[variable_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
  numeric(1)
)

# A preallocated loop makes the same repeated calculation explicit.
means_loop <- setNames(numeric(length(variables)), variables)
for (variable_name in variables) {
  means_loop[[variable_name]] <- mean(
    data[[variable_name]],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

stopifnot(
  identical(names(means_vapply), variables),
  isTRUE(all.equal(means_vapply, means_loop)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(means_vapply), summary_table$mean))
)

print(summary_table)
print(means_vapply)
cat("Week 12 vectorization and typed-iteration checks passed.\n")
```

</details>

**Explain / Check / Interpret:** Trace the first temperature: 67 F becomes about 19.4444 C. The reference
checks that value independently, then checks list/table order, missing counts
`37, 7, 0, 0`, and agreement between both mean implementations. `numeric(1)`
is an output template, not the value each mean must equal. Compare Ozone’s
`n_total = 153` with its 116 observed values; a mean alone hides this distinction.
The function does not promise to reject every nonfinite numeric input.

## Meeting 2 · Check the claim {#meeting-two}

The second reference uses the same data but adds a character `month_label`
column. It also **redefines** `summarize_numeric`: this version returns a status
and error-message column instead of a standard-deviation column. Run its full
reference block; do not mix the two function definitions. The safe wrapper
catches an expected error and returns a typed record so later requests can run.
An unavailable column is a failed task; an unavailable measurement is a value
inside a task. They need different evidence.

### One record per request, including failures {#stage-2}

**Slide cues:** *Include Expected Failures*; *Return A Typed Error Row*; *Check The Batch Log*; *Keep The Complete Log*.

Read `requested_variables` before running anything. `Ozone` and `Temp` are
numeric. `month_label` exists but is text, and `not_a_column` is absent. These
four requests test different branches; they are not four copies of a successful
Ozone test.

Inside `tryCatch`, the main expression calls the checked function. If it stops,
`error = function(error) ...` builds an error row using `conditionMessage`.
Both branches return the same column names and compatible types, including
numeric `mean` and character `error_message`. The error mean is unknown because
the task failed; it is not a measured zero. Filter successes into a **new** table
only after preserving and checking `run_log`.

**Predict in a private comment first:** What should the ordered status vector be for Ozone, month_label, not_a_column and Temp? How many rows should remain in the full log and in the successful-results table?

<details>
<summary>Compare your reasoning</summary>

The statuses are `ok, error, error, ok`. The full log has four rows and
the successful-results table has two. If your answer differed, you may have
treated a text column as an absent column, or confused a filtered analysis table
with the complete record of attempts.

</details>

**Try before expanding:** Use the Core 8 starter to write the success/error column names and types in a small skeleton before expanding. Keep the full log separate from the filtered successes.

<details>
<summary>Reference version · week12-repeated-workflow_sol.R</summary>

**Start a separate script for Meeting 2.** Both references use the name `summarize_numeric`, but this version returns `status` and `error_message` instead of `standard_deviation`. Close the Meeting 1 script and start from a fresh session before running this complete reference. Keep their tests and result columns with their respective versions; do not paste the two implementations into one script.

```{r}
#| label: w12-reference-2
# MATH 346 - possible worked solution
# Compare only after attempting the starter; other correct implementations are possible.

library(dplyr)

data <- airquality |>
  mutate(month_label = month.abb[Month])

summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("data must be a data frame")
  }
  if (!is.character(variable_name) || length(variable_name) != 1) {
    stop("variable_name must be one character value")
  }
  if (!variable_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("requested variable is not present")
  }

  values <- data[[variable_name]]
  if (!is.numeric(values)) {
    stop("requested variable must be numeric")
  }
  if (all(is.na(values))) {
    stop("requested variable has no observed values")
  }

  tibble(
    variable = variable_name,
    status = "ok",
    n_total = length(values),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(values)),
    mean = mean(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    error_message = NA_character_
  )
}

# Every request produces one status row, including failures.
safe_summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  tryCatch(
    summarize_numeric(data, variable_name),
    error = function(error) {
      tibble(
        variable = variable_name,
        status = "error",
        n_total = NA_integer_,
        n_missing = NA_integer_,
        mean = NA_real_,
        error_message = conditionMessage(error)
      )
    }
  )
}

requested_variables <- c(
  "Ozone",
  "month_label",
  "not_a_column",
  "Temp"
)

run_log <- bind_rows(lapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(variable_name) {
    safe_summarize_numeric(data, variable_name)
  }
))

stopifnot(
  nrow(run_log) == length(requested_variables),
  identical(run_log$variable, requested_variables),
  identical(run_log$status, c("ok", "error", "error", "ok")),
  all(nchar(run_log$error_message[run_log$status == "error"]) > 0),
  all(is.finite(run_log$mean[run_log$status == "ok"]))
)

successful_results <- run_log |>
  filter(status == "ok")

stopifnot(
  nrow(successful_results) == 2,
  identical(successful_results$variable, c("Ozone", "Temp"))
)

print(run_log)
cat("Week 12 repeated-workflow log preserves every request and failure.\n")
```

</details>

**Explain / Check / Interpret:** The source asserts input/output count, exact request order, two error
statuses, readable error messages and finite successful means. Inspect
`str(run_log)` too: a four-row table can still have a mean column coerced to
character. These are checks of the declared requests and supported inputs, not
a guarantee about untested files or arbitrary function arguments.

## AI audit · Inspect before accepting {#ai-audit}

**Slide cues:** *Dangerous Shortcut*; *Type Coercion Trap*; *AI Batch Audit*.

This is **selective Guided practice**; use it when selected or helpful.

Read the supplied target and choose a check before opening the diagnosis.
No AI service is contacted.

The two supplied variants use the same four requests. Choose between these
tests before the diagnosis: output count equals four; exact requested names and
order; mean values remain numeric; error rows have readable messages. Ask which
test each variant can pass while still being wrong.

**Reading excerpt:** this fragment relies on the supplied script setup; inspect it here, then run the complete file in the evidence reveal.

```r
generated_results <- bind_rows(lapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(variable_name) {
    tryCatch(
      tibble(
        variable = variable_name,
        mean = checked_mean(data, variable_name)
      ),
      error = function(error) NULL
    )
  }
))

generated_mixed <- sapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(variable_name) {
    tryCatch(
      checked_mean(data, variable_name),
      error = function(error) conditionMessage(error)
    )
  }
)
```


**Predict in a private comment first:** Which shortcut drops evidence, and which preserves four entries but changes successful numbers into text? Name a test that distinguishes the defects.

<details>
<summary>Compare your reasoning</summary>

`error = function(error) NULL` returns no record for a failed request;
`bind_rows` then produces only the two successes. Count and exact-name checks
expose it. The `sapply` variant mixes numbers with error strings and simplifies
them to a character vector. It preserves four names but fails the numeric-type
check. If your answer differed, you likely treated “four outputs” or “finished
without stopping” as a complete contract. A typed status row keeps the failed
request visible without converting successful means to text.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Run the complete supplied critique target and inspect the evidence</summary>

```{r}
#| label: w12-reference-ai
library(dplyr)

data <- airquality |>
  mutate(month_label = month.abb[Month])

checked_mean <- function(data, variable_name) {
  if (!variable_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("requested variable is not present")
  }

  values <- data[[variable_name]]
  if (!is.numeric(values)) {
    stop("requested variable must be numeric")
  }

  mean(values, na.rm = TRUE)
}

requested_variables <- c(
  "Ozone",
  "month_label",
  "not_a_column",
  "Temp"
)

# Generated batch code: an error becomes NULL and disappears in bind_rows().
generated_results <- bind_rows(lapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(variable_name) {
    tryCatch(
      tibble(
        variable = variable_name,
        mean = checked_mean(data, variable_name)
      ),
      error = function(error) NULL
    )
  }
))

stopifnot(
  nrow(generated_results) == 2,
  identical(generated_results$variable, c("Ozone", "Temp")),
  !all(requested_variables %in% generated_results$variable)
)

# Generated simplification: error messages force every numeric mean to text.
generated_mixed <- sapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(variable_name) {
    tryCatch(
      checked_mean(data, variable_name),
      error = function(error) conditionMessage(error)
    )
  }
)

stopifnot(
  is.character(generated_mixed),
  length(generated_mixed) == length(requested_variables),
  identical(names(generated_mixed), requested_variables),
  identical(generated_mixed[["not_a_column"]],
            "requested variable is not present")
)

cat("The generated batch silently drops two failed requests.\n")
cat("The generated simplification coerces valid numeric means to text.\n")
```

</details>

Use the existing AI policy when assistance is used: explain every accepted line
and keep the requested evidence with your existing work. A passing test never
replaces checking whether the code answers the actual question.

### Meeting 2 self-check · No submission

Close earlier reveals and explain from memory: A batch reports four rows in the correct order, but `typeof` says its mean
column is character. Has the batch contract passed? Explain what to inspect
before converting the column.

<details>
<summary>Compare the Meeting 2 self-check</summary>

No. Count and order passed, but numerical type did not. Inspect which
branch returned text, especially error handling, and restore compatible typed
success/error rows. Blind conversion can create fresh NAs and conceal the cause.
Retain the full log and use successful numeric rows separately.

</details>
